items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1995-11-14
items.q: I said Dizzy Gillespie and Louis Jordan broke up the big bands.

ctx.x: But were there any clubs that you tried to do this bebop that you could get a gig? No. There weren't any. Okay. So there weren't any.

The people didn't like the music, because they couldn't dance to it. But see, now that's the thing that really broke up the big bands. See, they had big bands to come and play. Now I said Dizzy Gillespie and Louis Jordan broke up the big bands. Dizzy Gillespie had a big band and the people couldn't dance to his music. So Louis Jordan came out with five pieces, and they would play music that people liked to hear and they would like to dance to. So the people would hire Louis Jordan, because he named but five…
Well I'm sure that was always a problem. When you were at Grunewald's, could you tell me what courses you taught? What classes? What, what, what, do you remember what classes?
